From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This is a **list of religious leaders who have been convicted of serious crimes** before, during or after their period as a religious leader.

## Violent crimes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Violent crimes")]

*   [Tony Alamo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alamo_Christian_Foundation "Alamo Christian Foundation") – Headed a Santa Clarita commune. Convicted of tax evasion in 1994 and then resided in a halfway house in [Texarkana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texarkana "Texarkana").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-1) In 2009, he was convicted of ten federal counts of taking minors across state lines for sex, and sentenced to 150 years in federal prison.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-2)
*   [Shoko Asahara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoko_Asahara "Shoko Asahara") – Founder of [Aum Shinrikyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aum_Shinrikyo "Aum Shinrikyo") sentenced to death by [hanging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanging "Hanging") under [Japanese law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_law "Japanese law") for involvement in the 1995 [Sarin gas attack on the Tokyo subway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarin_gas_attack_on_the_Tokyo_subway "Sarin gas attack on the Tokyo subway").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-3)
*   [Wayne Bent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Bent "Wayne Bent") (aka: Michael Travesser) – Founder of [Lord Our Righteousness Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord_Our_Righteousness_Church "Lord Our Righteousness Church"), sometimes called Strong City. Was convicted of one count of criminal sexual contact of a minor and two counts of contributing to the delinquency of a minor in 2008.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-4) He was sentenced to 18 years with eight years suspended.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-5)
*   [Graham Capill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graham_Capill "Graham Capill") – former leader of [Christian Heritage New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Heritage_New_Zealand "Christian Heritage New Zealand"). Sentenced to a nine-year imprisonment term in 2005 after multiple charges of child sexual abuse against girls younger than twelve.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-6)
*   [Matthew F. Hale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_F._Hale "Matthew F. Hale") – Former leader of [Creativity Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creativity_Movement "Creativity Movement") sentenced to a 40-year prison term for soliciting an undercover FBI informant to kill a federal judge.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-7)
*   [Ahmad Badreddin Hassoun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmad_Badreddin_Hassoun "Ahmad Badreddin Hassoun") – [Grand Mufti of Syria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Mufti_of_Syria "Grand Mufti of Syria") from 2005 until 2021. Sentenced to life imprisonment following the [fall of the Assad regime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_of_the_Assad_regime "Fall of the Assad regime") for crimes including "inciting civil war and sectarian strife", incitement to murder and abuse of office.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-8)
*   [Warren Jeffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Jeffs "Warren Jeffs") – Once President of [Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundamentalist_Church_of_Jesus_Christ_of_Latter_Day_Saints "Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints") (a polygamist Mormon sect), convicted of rape as an accomplice (overturned in 2010). Jeffs was convicted in a Texas state court of child sex charges and sentenced to life plus 20 years. He is incarcerated at the Powledge state prison. He also awaits trial in other states and in the federal court system.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-9)
*   [Jung Myung-seok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jung_Myung-seok "Jung Myung-seok") – South Korean religious sect leader and founder of [Providence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence_(religion) "Providence (religion)"). Convicted for raping several of his followers.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-10)
*   [William Kamm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Kamm "William Kamm") – An Australian religious sect leader who was sentenced to prison in October 2005 for a string of sexual attacks on a 15-year-old girl. In August 2007 his sentence was increased after being found guilty for a series of sexual abuses against another teenage girl over a five-year period.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-11)
*   [Ervil LeBaron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ervil_LeBaron "Ervil LeBaron") – Led a small sect of [polygamous Mormon fundamentalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygamous_Mormon_fundamentalists "Polygamous Mormon fundamentalists"), and was convicted of involvement in the murder of two people and plotting to kill another person in 1981.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-12)
*   [Alice Lenshina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_Lenshina "Alice Lenshina") – Zambian head and founder of the [Lumpa Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lumpa_Church "Lumpa Church"). Conflicts with the government over the sect's rejection of taxes led to a violent confrontation and her subsequent imprisonment.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-13)
*   [Jeffrey Lundgren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_Lundgren "Jeffrey Lundgren") – Headed splinter group from [Reorganized Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reorganized_Church_of_Jesus_Christ_of_Latter_Day_Saints "Reorganized Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints"), executed on October 24, 2006, for multiple murders.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-14)
*   [Charles Manson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Manson "Charles Manson") – Leader of the [Manson Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manson_Family "Manson Family") who served life in prison for [first-degree murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder_in_United_States_law "Murder in United States law") until his death in 2017.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-15)
*   [Shukri Mustafa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shukri_Mustafa "Shukri Mustafa") – Egyptian leader of [Takfir wal-Hijra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takfir_wal-Hijra "Takfir wal-Hijra") who was captured and executed on March 19, 1978, for the kidnapping and murder of an Egyptian ex-government minister.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-16)
*   [Fred Phelps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Phelps "Fred Phelps") – Leader of anti-gay [Westboro Baptist Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westboro_Baptist_Church "Westboro Baptist Church"). Convicted for disorderly conduct and battery.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-18)
*   [Swami Premananda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swami_Premananda_(guru) "Swami Premananda (guru)") – Indian religious leader convicted and sentenced to two life sentences for the rape of 13 girls and murder in 2005.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-19)
*   [Theodore Rinaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodore_Rinaldo "Theodore Rinaldo") – Leader of a religious group in [Snohomish, Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snohomish,_Washington "Snohomish, Washington") convicted of third-degree statutory rape for having sexual intercourse with one minor girl and of taking indecent liberties with another.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-20)
*   [Keith Raniere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Raniere "Keith Raniere") – The founder of NXIVM, a multi-level marketing company and cult based near Albany, New York. Raniere was convicted of racketeering on the charges of sex trafficking, sexual exploitation of a child, attempted sex trafficking, identity theft, forced labor, conspiracy to alter records, conspiracy of sex trafficking, forced labor, racketeering, and wire fraud. Raniere was sentenced to 120 years in federal prison starting in January 2021.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-22)
*   [Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gurmeet_Ram_Rahim_Singh "Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh") – an Indian guru, music producer, singer-songwriter, actor, and filmmaker. He has been the head of the social group [Dera Sacha Sauda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dera_Sacha_Sauda "Dera Sacha Sauda") since 1990. On 28 August 2017, Singh was sentenced to 20 years in jail for rape.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-23) He has also faced prosecution for murder and ordering forced castrations. He is also alleged to have committed sexual assaults on many of his followers. He is also alleged to be involved in the murder of a journalist[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-24)
*   [Flordelis dos Santos de Souza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flordelis_dos_Santos_de_Souza "Flordelis dos Santos de Souza") – Brazilian former Pentecostal pastor, gospel singer and politician. In 2022, she was convicted of murder of her husband, Anderson do Carmo.
*   [Paul Schäfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Sch%C3%A4fer "Paul Schäfer") – Former head of Chile-based [Colonia Dignidad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonia_Dignidad "Colonia Dignidad"), was convicted of sexually abusing 25 children.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-25)
*   [Joseph Smith, Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Smith "Joseph Smith") – The founder of the [Latter Day Saint movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latter_Day_Saint_movement "Latter Day Saint movement"), was "subjected to approximately thirty criminal actions" during his life. Another source reports [Smith was arrested at least 42 times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Smith_and_the_criminal_justice_system "Joseph Smith and the criminal justice system").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-26) A year after committing assault and battery on a local official,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-27) Smith was [killed by a mob](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_of_Joseph_Smith "Death of Joseph Smith") while in jail awaiting trial on charges of treason against Illinois.
*   [Roch Thériault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roch_Th%C3%A9riault "Roch Thériault") – Former head of "Ant Hill Kids commune" served a [life sentence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_sentence "Life sentence") in Canada for the murder of Solange Boislard.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-28)
*   [Yahweh ben Yahweh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yahweh_ben_Yahweh "Yahweh ben Yahweh") – Head of [Nation of Yahweh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nation_of_Yahweh "Nation of Yahweh"), convicted for [Federal racketeering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racketeer_Influenced_and_Corrupt_Organizations_Act "Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act") charges and conspiracy involving 14 murders.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-29)
*   [Dwight York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_York "Dwight York") – Head of [Nuwaubianism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuwaubianism "Nuwaubianism"), convicted in 2004 of multiple [RICO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RICO "RICO"), child molestation, and financial reporting charges and sentenced to 135 years in prison.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-30)

## Non-violent crimes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Non-violent crimes")]

*   [Jim Bakker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Bakker "Jim Bakker") – Created the [PTL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_PTL_Club "The PTL Club") (Praise the Lord) organization. Convicted of [fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraud "Fraud") and conspiracy charges after illegally soliciting millions of dollars from his followers.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-31)
*   [David Yonggi Cho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yonggi_Cho "David Yonggi Cho") – Founder of [Yoido Full Gospel Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoido_Full_Gospel_Church "Yoido Full Gospel Church"). Sentenced to three years in prison in 2014 for embezzling 13 billion won (US$12 million) in church funds.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-32)
*   [Joseph Di Mambro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Di_Mambro "Joseph Di Mambro") – A founder of the [Order of the Solar Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Solar_Temple "Order of the Solar Temple"). Several years prior to founding the group, he was convicted of fraud, impersonating a psychiatrist, and writing bad checks.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-33)
*   [William R. Ferguson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_R._Ferguson "William R. Ferguson") – Founder of the [Cosmic Circle of Fellowship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosmic_Circle_of_Fellowship "Cosmic Circle of Fellowship"). Prior to the founding of the group, he was sentenced to two years in prison for selling a quack healing device called the "Zerret Applicator".[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-ThePalladium-Item1949-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-ChicagoDailyTribune1950e-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-36)
*   [Hogen Fukunaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hogen_Fukunaga "Hogen Fukunaga") – Founder of [Ho No Hana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ho_No_Hana "Ho No Hana") who was given a twelve-year jail sentence for fraudulently gaining 150 million [yen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yen "Yen") from his followers.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-37)
*   [Kent Hovind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kent_Hovind "Kent Hovind") (Dr. Dino) – founder of the Creation Science Evangelism ministry. Willful failure to collect, account for, and pay over Federal income taxes, knowingly structuring transactions in Federally insured financial institutions to evade the reporting requirements, and obstructing and impeding the administration of the internal revenue laws.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-39)
*   [L. Ron Hubbard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L._Ron_Hubbard "L. Ron Hubbard") – Founder of [Scientology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientology "Scientology"). He was convicted of petty theft and ordered to pay a $25 fine in San Luis Obispo, California, in 1948[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-Miller-142-40) and in 1978 was convicted of illegal business practices, namely, making false claims about his ability to cure physical illnesses in France. He was convicted in Canadian Federal Court of conspiring to buy illegal handguns.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-46)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This is a **list of religious leaders who have been convicted of serious crimes** before, during or after their period as a religious leader.

## Violent crimes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Violent crimes")]

*   [Tony Alamo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alamo_Christian_Foundation "Alamo Christian Foundation") – Headed a Santa Clarita commune. Convicted of tax evasion in 1994 and then resided in a halfway house in [Texarkana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texarkana "Texarkana").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-1) In 2009, he was convicted of ten federal counts of taking minors across state lines for sex, and sentenced to 150 years in federal prison.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-2)
*   [Shoko Asahara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoko_Asahara "Shoko Asahara") – Founder of [Aum Shinrikyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aum_Shinrikyo "Aum Shinrikyo") sentenced to death by [hanging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanging "Hanging") under [Japanese law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_law "Japanese law") for involvement in the 1995 [Sarin gas attack on the Tokyo subway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarin_gas_attack_on_the_Tokyo_subway "Sarin gas attack on the Tokyo subway").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-3)
*   [Wayne Bent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Bent "Wayne Bent") (aka: Michael Travesser) – Founder of [Lord Our Righteousness Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord_Our_Righteousness_Church "Lord Our Righteousness Church"), sometimes called Strong City. Was convicted of one count of criminal sexual contact of a minor and two counts of contributing to the delinquency of a minor in 2008.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-4) He was sentenced to 18 years with eight years suspended.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-5)
*   [Graham Capill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graham_Capill "Graham Capill") – former leader of [Christian Heritage New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Heritage_New_Zealand "Christian Heritage New Zealand"). Sentenced to a nine-year imprisonment term in 2005 after multiple charges of child sexual abuse against girls younger than twelve.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-6)
*   [Matthew F. Hale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_F._Hale "Matthew F. Hale") – Former leader of [Creativity Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creativity_Movement "Creativity Movement") sentenced to a 40-year prison term for soliciting an undercover FBI informant to kill a federal judge.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-7)
*   [Ahmad Badreddin Hassoun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmad_Badreddin_Hassoun "Ahmad Badreddin Hassoun") – [Grand Mufti of Syria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Mufti_of_Syria "Grand Mufti of Syria") from 2005 until 2021. Sentenced to life imprisonment following the [fall of the Assad regime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_of_the_Assad_regime "Fall of the Assad regime") for crimes including "inciting civil war and sectarian strife", incitement to murder and abuse of office.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-8)
*   [Warren Jeffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Jeffs "Warren Jeffs") – Once President of [Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundamentalist_Church_of_Jesus_Christ_of_Latter_Day_Saints "Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints") (a polygamist Mormon sect), convicted of rape as an accomplice (overturned in 2010). Jeffs was convicted in a Texas state court of child sex charges and sentenced to life plus 20 years. He is incarcerated at the Powledge state prison. He also awaits trial in other states and in the federal court system.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-9)
*   [Jung Myung-seok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jung_Myung-seok "Jung Myung-seok") – South Korean religious sect leader and founder of [Providence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence_(religion) "Providence (religion)"). Convicted for raping several of his followers.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-10)
*   [William Kamm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Kamm "William Kamm") – An Australian religious sect leader who was sentenced to prison in October 2005 for a string of sexual attacks on a 15-year-old girl. In August 2007 his sentence was increased after being found guilty for a series of sexual abuses against another teenage girl over a five-year period.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-11)
*   [Ervil LeBaron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ervil_LeBaron "Ervil LeBaron") – Led a small sect of [polygamous Mormon fundamentalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygamous_Mormon_fundamentalists "Polygamous Mormon fundamentalists"), and was convicted of involvement in the murder of two people and plotting to kill another person in 1981.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-12)
*   [Alice Lenshina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_Lenshina "Alice Lenshina") – Zambian head and founder of the [Lumpa Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lumpa_Church "Lumpa Church"). Conflicts with the government over the sect's rejection of taxes led to a violent confrontation and her subsequent imprisonment.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-13)
*   [Jeffrey Lundgren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_Lundgren "Jeffrey Lundgren") – Headed splinter group from [Reorganized Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reorganized_Church_of_Jesus_Christ_of_Latter_Day_Saints "Reorganized Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints"), executed on October 24, 2006, for multiple murders.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-14)
*   [Charles Manson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Manson "Charles Manson") – Leader of the [Manson Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manson_Family "Manson Family") who served life in prison for [first-degree murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder_in_United_States_law "Murder in United States law") until his death in 2017.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes#cite_note-15)

**Kong Hee** ([Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language"):康希; [pinyin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinyin "Pinyin"):_Kāng Xī_; born 23 August 1964) is the founder and senior pastor of [City Harvest Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Harvest_Church "City Harvest Church").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-BioKongHee-2)

He was convicted in 2015 of being involved in the [City Harvest Church Criminal Breach of Trust Case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Harvest_Church_Criminal_Breach_of_Trust_Case "City Harvest Church Criminal Breach of Trust Case"), Singapore's biggest case in misuse of charitable funds.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-5) He was seen to be the "key man" behind the scandal[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-6) who had guided his five accomplices by the Singapore court of three charges of criminal breach of trust.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-guilty-7) Although Kong and the five were guilty of serious breaches, the court noted that the $50 million was also ultimately returned to the church.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-defence-nowrongfulgain-8)

He served his sentence at Changi Prison Complex from 21 April 2017 to 22 August 2019.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-needtoknow-10)

Kong is also involved in the Christian [Charismatic Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charismatic_Movement "Charismatic Movement"), a philosophy of ministry that emphasises the [Great Commandment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Commandment "Great Commandment"), the [Great Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Commission "Great Commission") and the [Cultural Mandate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_Mandate "Cultural Mandate").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-11)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Kong is the fifth child of Kong Leng, a [professional engineer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_engineer "Professional engineer"), and Toh Poh-Eng, a diamond trader. From 1975 to 1988, Kong was a member of [Marine Parade Christian Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_Parade_Christian_Centre?action=edit&redlink=1 "Marine Parade Christian Centre (page does not exist)"), an [Anglican church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglican_church "Anglican church") located in eastern Singapore. He studied at [Raffles Institution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raffles_Institution "Raffles Institution") (1977–1981), [Raffles Junior College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raffles_Junior_College "Raffles Junior College") (1982) as well as [National University of Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_Singapore "National University of Singapore"), [Bachelor of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") (Computer & Information Sciences) (1985–1988).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

During his university years, he worked part-time for the [Chapel of the Resurrection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapel_of_the_Resurrection "Chapel of the Resurrection") under the oversight of Anglican vicar, Reverend Dr. [Canon James Wong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canon_James_Wong?action=edit&redlink=1 "Canon James Wong (page does not exist)"). During that tenure, he helped Canon Wong set up a new congregation, [Orchard Christian Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orchard_Christian_Centre?action=edit&redlink=1 "Orchard Christian Centre (page does not exist)"). Upon university graduation in 1988, Kong worked a short stint in a local publishing house as a programmer.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1989, Kong was a staff evangelist with "[Christ For Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christ_For_Asia?action=edit&redlink=1 "Christ For Asia (page does not exist)")", a missions organisation in the [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines "Philippines") led by [Assemblies of God](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assemblies_of_God "Assemblies of God") minister, Reverend [Randy Sing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Sing?action=edit&redlink=1 "Randy Sing (page does not exist)"). At that same time, there was an opportunity for Kong to pioneer a new church in Singapore. With the support and encouragement of some senior pastors in the city, Kong decided to relocate back to Singapore and helped set up a new congregation with 20 youths.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-BioKongHee-2)

## City Harvest Church

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: City Harvest Church")]

Main article: [City Harvest Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Harvest_Church "City Harvest Church")

On 7 May 1989, City Harvest Church was founded as a department (known as "Ekklesia Ministry") of Bethany Christian Centre (Assemblies of God).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-12)

From 1997, Kong was the executive director of the [Festival of Praise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Festival_of_Praise "Festival of Praise"), an annual event that brought together churches for united prayer and worship.[_[needs update?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Dates\_and\_numbers#Chronological\_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_] Kong was a board member of Dr. [David Yonggi Cho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yonggi_Cho "David Yonggi Cho")'s [Church Growth International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_Growth_International?action=edit&redlink=1 "Church Growth International (page does not exist)") (South Korea) and Dr. [Luis Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Bush "Luis Bush")'s Transform World (Indonesia). Kong is a protege,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-13) friend and mentee[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-14) of [Phil Pringle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Pringle "Phil Pringle"), the founder and senior pastor of [C3 Church Global](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C3_Church_Global "C3 Church Global") (Australia) and advisory pastor to City Harvest Church.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-15) With his wife [Sun Ho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Ho "Sun Ho"), they once owned two companies, [International Harvest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Harvest?action=edit&redlink=1 "International Harvest (page does not exist)") and [Skin Couture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin_Couture?action=edit&redlink=1 "Skin Couture (page does not exist)").

In December 2010, City Harvest Church had an average of 23,256 attendees[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-CHCStory-16) with 47 affiliate "Harvest" churches, as well as 29 affiliate churches and 6 Bible schools in Asia, namely, in Singapore, Australia, Indonesia, Malaysia and Taiwan. Another 18 affiliate churches in East and West Malaysia are under the [Malaysian Harvest Fellowship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysian_Harvest_Fellowship?action=edit&redlink=1 "Malaysian Harvest Fellowship (page does not exist)") which Kong Hee co-founded.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-20)

## Conviction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Conviction")]

Main article: [City Harvest Church Criminal Breach of Trust Case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Harvest_Church_Criminal_Breach_of_Trust_Case "City Harvest Church Criminal Breach of Trust Case")

### Investigations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Investigations")]

On 31 May 2010, the Office of the Commissioner of Charities and the [Commercial Affairs Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commercial_Affairs_Department "Commercial Affairs Department") of the Singapore Police began investigating more than 16 individuals linked to City Harvest Church, including church founder Kong Hee and his wife, [Sun Ho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Ho "Sun Ho").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-22) The police were looking into financial transactions involving the possible falsification of accounts and criminal breach of trust amounting to millions of dollars which dated back a number of years. The authorities allowed regular church activities and services to continue for the congregation during ongoing investigations.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-27)

On 26 June 2012, the Commissioner of Charities released a press statement detailing the results of its inquiry. It stated that there were misconduct and mismanagement in the administration of City Harvest Church. There were irregularities of at least $23 million in the church's funds, which were used to finance [Sun Ho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ho_Yeow_Sun "Ho Yeow Sun")'s secular music career. There was also a concerted effort to conceal this movement of funds from stakeholders. Kong Hee and seven others were suspended from their roles in the church.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-28)

A subsequent report indicated that the investigations were trigged by complaints made to the authorities.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-29)

### Arrests and charges

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Arrests and charges")]

Also on 26 June 2012, Kong Hee and four other leaders of City Harvest Church were arrested and charged with misuse of funds.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-31) A sixth leader was charged on 25 July 2012. All six accused were granted bail of S$500,000 and had their passports impounded.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-32)

### Trial and conviction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Trial and conviction")]

The trial of Kong Hee and the five other leaders commenced in May 2013 and was adjourned several times.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-35) There was a total of 142 days of hearings.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-36)

The verdicts were announced on 21 October 2015. Kong Hee and the other five leaders were found guilty of all charges.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-guilty-7)

Sentencing was on 20 November 2015. Kong Hee received the heaviest sentence of the six, 8 years in prison.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-38) Following a request from the defendants, the judge agreed to defer the start of the sentences until 11 January 2016.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-40)

### Related decisions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Related decisions")]

In 2017, the Commissioner of Charities permanently barred the six in the case, with two additional church executive members, [Kelvin Teo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelvin_Teo "Kelvin Teo") Meng How and Tan Su Pheng Jacqueline, from holding key management positions or being a board member in City Harvest Church or any other charity. Additionally the church was barred from paying the legal fees for the six. However, they were still allowed to perform their religious activities.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-41)

### Appeals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Appeals")]

On 27 November 2015, it was reported that the Attorney General's Chambers had filed appeals against the sentence issued to Kong Hee and the five other defendants, on the grounds that it was "manifestly inadequate".[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-42)

On 2 December 2015, it was reported that Kong Hee and the other five defendants had also filed appeals.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-43)

On 4 March 2016, it was reported that the appeal hearing would commence on 19 September 2016.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-44)

On 7 April 2017, his original sentence of 8 years in prison was reduced to 3.5 years.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-45) In delivering their decision, the judges noted that there was no element of wrongful gain or personal financial benefit, either direct or indirect.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-defence-nowrongfulgain2-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-48) The Court of Appeal acknowledged that “The theological legitimacy of the Crossover as a means of evangelism is not an issue in this case.” (Para 1)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-Inquiry-Misconduct-49) “The Crossover – which is central to the entire case – is an evangelistic endeavour to spread the gospel through the secular music of Sun Ho. It is not disputed that the Crossover had the full support of the CHC Board.” (Para 21)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-Inquiry-Misconduct-49)

Pages 264-267 of the appeal judgement characterised Kong as "coloured by greed and self-interest", as the Crossover project appeared to have been designed to benefit Sun Ho and Kong Hee. Sun Ho's contract with Xtron (a company controlled by Kong Hee) was to entitle Sun to 25% of gross income (estimated to reach US$30M[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]) regardless of project costs, in addition to a monthly salary of US$10,000.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-50) However, this contract between Sun Ho and Xtron was terminated in August 2008.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-51)

In addition, he had told members they were off-salary from the church. A private fund was set up to and raised over $3 million “to fund the [Crossover] Project” and was fully expended in just 3 years for the purposes of the Project.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-Inquiry-Misconduct-49)

Kong Hee began serving his sentence on 21 April 2017.

### Comments by the Minister for Law

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Comments by the Minister for Law")]

| External videos |
| --- |
| [![Image 5: video icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg/20px-Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg)[Law minister K Shanmugam setting out the government's position on the court's ruling](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QDiuG2HTHOo), Gov.sg video |

Expressing his disappointment by the Court of Appeal's decision to overrule a 1976 High Court decision, which had held that company directors could be convicted for criminal breach of trust under section 409 of the Penal Code, [Minister for Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_for_Law "Minister for Law")[K Shanmugam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K_Shanmugam "K Shanmugam") said, “The government believes the sentences are too low. But the sentences reflect the law as it stands after the High Court’s decision last year confirmed by the Court of Appeal. The courts decide these matters. All of us have to respect the decision regardless of whether we agree or disagree with it.”

“It is now up to Parliament to amend the law, and that we should do soon. We will ensure that legislation provides for higher penalties for directors and other senior officers who commit criminal breach of trust,” he added.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-52)

### Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Release")]

On 22 August 2019, Kong Hee was released from prison, having served 2 years and 4 months of the sentence.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-53) Inmates typically serve two-thirds of their sentence before released on remission for good behaviour.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-54)

In his first appearance at the church after his release, Kong delivered a four-minute speech apologising to church members for "any pain, anxiety, disappointment, or grief that you have suffered because of me".[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-55)

## Controversies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Controversies")]

### Plagiarism

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Plagiarism")]

In March 2010, a blogger identified plagiarism on Kong Hee's _Daily Devotionals_ as they were similar to writings in another publication, _[The Leadership Bible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Leadership\_Bible?action=edit&redlink=1 "The Leadership Bible (page does not exist)")_ which had been published ten years prior. The copied text were published as physical copies into two books, _[Renewing Your Spiritual Energy in 90 Days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renewing\_Your\_Spiritual\_Energy\_in\_90\_Days?action=edit&redlink=1 "Renewing Your Spiritual Energy in 90 Days (page does not exist)")_, without accreditation to the original authors. Kong Hee's daily devotionals were originally compiled from his personal reading notes and printed as supplementary reading for his members, free of charge. Some years later, due to popular demand overseas, a local publisher compiled and released foreign language translations of the devotional for sale.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Kong Hee posted a note on his website and explained that the devotion was "originally meant only for internal circulation among the members of my church. As such, there was an oversight in not quoting the sources of some portions that borrow from the writings of other Christian authors." There was also an apology for the oversight.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-ST-plagiarisedBook-57)

The publisher, who is also a member of City Harvest Church, acknowledged that at the time of publication, both himself and Mr Kong were aware that certain portions of the content were not original.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-ST-plagiarisedBook-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-58) The publisher of "Renewal" has since made amendments to the soft copies to include accreditation.

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Kong is married to pastor-turned-pop-singer [Ho Yeow Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ho_Yeow_Sun "Ho Yeow Sun"), also known as Sun Ho. They have one son, Dayan Kong, who was born in 2005.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-59)

Kong was the co-owner of a 5,242 sq ft duplex penthouse located on the 11th floor of The Oceanfront in the premium residential enclave [Sentosa Cove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentosa_Cove "Sentosa Cove"). The penthouse was co-owned with Indonesian tycoon Mr Wahju Hanafi, a church follower. The pair bought the penthouse for $9.33 million in 2007, each paying monthly installments of $17,000, before the apartment was sold at a loss of over S$2 million to a Kenyan diplomat.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-60)

**Kong Hee** ([Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language"):康希; [pinyin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinyin "Pinyin"):_Kāng Xī_; born 23 August 1964) is the founder and senior pastor of [City Harvest Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Harvest_Church "City Harvest Church").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-BioKongHee-2)

He was convicted in 2015 of being involved in the [City Harvest Church Criminal Breach of Trust Case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Harvest_Church_Criminal_Breach_of_Trust_Case "City Harvest Church Criminal Breach of Trust Case"), Singapore's biggest case in misuse of charitable funds.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-5) He was seen to be the "key man" behind the scandal[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-6) who had guided his five accomplices by the Singapore court of three charges of criminal breach of trust.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-guilty-7) Although Kong and the five were guilty of serious breaches, the court noted that the $50 million was also ultimately returned to the church.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-defence-nowrongfulgain-8)

He served his sentence at Changi Prison Complex from 21 April 2017 to 22 August 2019.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-needtoknow-10)

Kong is also involved in the Christian [Charismatic Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charismatic_Movement "Charismatic Movement"), a philosophy of ministry that emphasises the [Great Commandment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Commandment "Great Commandment"), the [Great Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Commission "Great Commission") and the [Cultural Mandate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_Mandate "Cultural Mandate").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-11)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Kong is the fifth child of Kong Leng, a [professional engineer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_engineer "Professional engineer"), and Toh Poh-Eng, a diamond trader. From 1975 to 1988, Kong was a member of [Marine Parade Christian Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_Parade_Christian_Centre?action=edit&redlink=1 "Marine Parade Christian Centre (page does not exist)"), an [Anglican church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglican_church "Anglican church") located in eastern Singapore. He studied at [Raffles Institution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raffles_Institution "Raffles Institution") (1977–1981), [Raffles Junior College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raffles_Junior_College "Raffles Junior College") (1982) as well as [National University of Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_Singapore "National University of Singapore"), [Bachelor of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") (Computer & Information Sciences) (1985–1988).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

During his university years, he worked part-time for the [Chapel of the Resurrection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapel_of_the_Resurrection "Chapel of the Resurrection") under the oversight of Anglican vicar, Reverend Dr. [Canon James Wong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canon_James_Wong?action=edit&redlink=1 "Canon James Wong (page does not exist)"). During that tenure, he helped Canon Wong set up a new congregation, [Orchard Christian Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orchard_Christian_Centre?action=edit&redlink=1 "Orchard Christian Centre (page does not exist)"). Upon university graduation in 1988, Kong worked a short stint in a local publishing house as a programmer.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1989, Kong was a staff evangelist with "[Christ For Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christ_For_Asia?action=edit&redlink=1 "Christ For Asia (page does not exist)")", a missions organisation in the [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines "Philippines") led by [Assemblies of God](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assemblies_of_God "Assemblies of God") minister, Reverend [Randy Sing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Sing?action=edit&redlink=1 "Randy Sing (page does not exist)"). At that same time, there was an opportunity for Kong to pioneer a new church in Singapore. With the support and encouragement of some senior pastors in the city, Kong decided to relocate back to Singapore and helped set up a new congregation with 20 youths.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-BioKongHee-2)

## City Harvest Church

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: City Harvest Church")]

Main article: [City Harvest Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Harvest_Church "City Harvest Church")

On 7 May 1989, City Harvest Church was founded as a department (known as "Ekklesia Ministry") of Bethany Christian Centre (Assemblies of God).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-12)

From 1997, Kong was the executive director of the [Festival of Praise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Festival_of_Praise "Festival of Praise"), an annual event that brought together churches for united prayer and worship.[_[needs update?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Dates\_and\_numbers#Chronological\_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_] Kong was a board member of Dr. [David Yonggi Cho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yonggi_Cho "David Yonggi Cho")'s [Church Growth International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_Growth_International?action=edit&redlink=1 "Church Growth International (page does not exist)") (South Korea) and Dr. [Luis Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Bush "Luis Bush")'s Transform World (Indonesia). Kong is a protege,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-13) friend and mentee[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-14) of [Phil Pringle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Pringle "Phil Pringle"), the founder and senior pastor of [C3 Church Global](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C3_Church_Global "C3 Church Global") (Australia) and advisory pastor to City Harvest Church.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-15) With his wife [Sun Ho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Ho "Sun Ho"), they once owned two companies, [International Harvest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Harvest?action=edit&redlink=1 "International Harvest (page does not exist)") and [Skin Couture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin_Couture?action=edit&redlink=1 "Skin Couture (page does not exist)").

In December 2010, City Harvest Church had an average of 23,256 attendees[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-CHCStory-16) with 47 affiliate "Harvest" churches, as well as 29 affiliate churches and 6 Bible schools in Asia, namely, in Singapore, Australia, Indonesia, Malaysia and Taiwan. Another 18 affiliate churches in East and West Malaysia are under the [Malaysian Harvest Fellowship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysian_Harvest_Fellowship?action=edit&redlink=1 "Malaysian Harvest Fellowship (page does not exist)") which Kong Hee co-founded.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-20)

## Conviction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Conviction")]

Main article: [City Harvest Church Criminal Breach of Trust Case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Harvest_Church_Criminal_Breach_of_Trust_Case "City Harvest Church Criminal Breach of Trust Case")

### Investigations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Investigations")]

On 31 May 2010, the Office of the Commissioner of Charities and the [Commercial Affairs Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commercial_Affairs_Department "Commercial Affairs Department") of the Singapore Police began investigating more than 16 individuals linked to City Harvest Church, including church founder Kong Hee and his wife, [Sun Ho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Ho "Sun Ho").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-22) The police were looking into financial transactions involving the possible falsification of accounts and criminal breach of trust amounting to millions of dollars which dated back a number of years. The authorities allowed regular church activities and services to continue for the congregation during ongoing investigations.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-27)

On 26 June 2012, the Commissioner of Charities released a press statement detailing the results of its inquiry. It stated that there were misconduct and mismanagement in the administration of City Harvest Church. There were irregularities of at least $23 million in the church's funds, which were used to finance [Sun Ho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ho_Yeow_Sun "Ho Yeow Sun")'s secular music career. There was also a concerted effort to conceal this movement of funds from stakeholders. Kong Hee and seven others were suspended from their roles in the church.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-28)

A subsequent report indicated that the investigations were trigged by complaints made to the authorities.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-29)

### Arrests and charges

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Arrests and charges")]

Also on 26 June 2012, Kong Hee and four other leaders of City Harvest Church were arrested and charged with misuse of funds.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-31) A sixth leader was charged on 25 July 2012. All six accused were granted bail of S$500,000 and had their passports impounded.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-32)

### Trial and conviction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Trial and conviction")]

The trial of Kong Hee and the five other leaders commenced in May 2013 and was adjourned several times.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-35) There was a total of 142 days of hearings.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-36)

The verdicts were announced on 21 October 2015. Kong Hee and the other five leaders were found guilty of all charges.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-guilty-7)

Sentencing was on 20 November 2015. Kong Hee received the heaviest sentence of the six, 8 years in prison.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-38) Following a request from the defendants, the judge agreed to defer the start of the sentences until 11 January 2016.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-40)

### Related decisions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Related decisions")]

In 2017, the Commissioner of Charities permanently barred the six in the case, with two additional church executive members, [Kelvin Teo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelvin_Teo "Kelvin Teo") Meng How and Tan Su Pheng Jacqueline, from holding key management positions or being a board member in City Harvest Church or any other charity. Additionally the church was barred from paying the legal fees for the six. However, they were still allowed to perform their religious activities.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-41)

### Appeals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Appeals")]

On 27 November 2015, it was reported that the Attorney General's Chambers had filed appeals against the sentence issued to Kong Hee and the five other defendants, on the grounds that it was "manifestly inadequate".[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-42)

On 2 December 2015, it was reported that Kong Hee and the other five defendants had also filed appeals.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-43)

On 4 March 2016, it was reported that the appeal hearing would commence on 19 September 2016.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-44)

On 7 April 2017, his original sentence of 8 years in prison was reduced to 3.5 years.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-45) In delivering their decision, the judges noted that there was no element of wrongful gain or personal financial benefit, either direct or indirect.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-defence-nowrongfulgain2-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-48) The Court of Appeal acknowledged that “The theological legitimacy of the Crossover as a means of evangelism is not an issue in this case.” (Para 1)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-Inquiry-Misconduct-49) “The Crossover – which is central to the entire case – is an evangelistic endeavour to spread the gospel through the secular music of Sun Ho. It is not disputed that the Crossover had the full support of the CHC Board.” (Para 21)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-Inquiry-Misconduct-49)

Pages 264-267 of the appeal judgement characterised Kong as "coloured by greed and self-interest", as the Crossover project appeared to have been designed to benefit Sun Ho and Kong Hee. Sun Ho's contract with Xtron (a company controlled by Kong Hee) was to entitle Sun to 25% of gross income (estimated to reach US$30M[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]) regardless of project costs, in addition to a monthly salary of US$10,000.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-50) However, this contract between Sun Ho and Xtron was terminated in August 2008.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-51)

In addition, he had told members they were off-salary from the church. A private fund was set up to and raised over $3 million “to fund the [Crossover] Project” and was fully expended in just 3 years for the purposes of the Project.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-Inquiry-Misconduct-49)

Kong Hee began serving his sentence on 21 April 2017.

### Comments by the Minister for Law

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Comments by the Minister for Law")]

| External videos |
| --- |
| [![Image 5: video icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg/20px-Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg)[Law minister K Shanmugam setting out the government's position on the court's ruling](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QDiuG2HTHOo), Gov.sg video |

Expressing his disappointment by the Court of Appeal's decision to overrule a 1976 High Court decision, which had held that company directors could be convicted for criminal breach of trust under section 409 of the Penal Code, [Minister for Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_for_Law "Minister for Law")[K Shanmugam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K_Shanmugam "K Shanmugam") said, “The government believes the sentences are too low. But the sentences reflect the law as it stands after the High Court’s decision last year confirmed by the Court of Appeal. The courts decide these matters. All of us have to respect the decision regardless of whether we agree or disagree with it.”

“It is now up to Parliament to amend the law, and that we should do soon. We will ensure that legislation provides for higher penalties for directors and other senior officers who commit criminal breach of trust,” he added.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-52)

### Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Release")]

On 22 August 2019, Kong Hee was released from prison, having served 2 years and 4 months of the sentence.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-53) Inmates typically serve two-thirds of their sentence before released on remission for good behaviour.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-54)

In his first appearance at the church after his release, Kong delivered a four-minute speech apologising to church members for "any pain, anxiety, disappointment, or grief that you have suffered because of me".[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-55)

## Controversies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Controversies")]

### Plagiarism

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Plagiarism")]

In March 2010, a blogger identified plagiarism on Kong Hee's _Daily Devotionals_ as they were similar to writings in another publication, _[The Leadership Bible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Leadership\_Bible?action=edit&redlink=1 "The Leadership Bible (page does not exist)")_ which had been published ten years prior. The copied text were published as physical copies into two books, _[Renewing Your Spiritual Energy in 90 Days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renewing\_Your\_Spiritual\_Energy\_in\_90\_Days?action=edit&redlink=1 "Renewing Your Spiritual Energy in 90 Days (page does not exist)")_, without accreditation to the original authors. Kong Hee's daily devotionals were originally compiled from his personal reading notes and printed as supplementary reading for his members, free of charge. Some years later, due to popular demand overseas, a local publisher compiled and released foreign language translations of the devotional for sale.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Kong Hee posted a note on his website and explained that the devotion was "originally meant only for internal circulation among the members of my church. As such, there was an oversight in not quoting the sources of some portions that borrow from the writings of other Christian authors." There was also an apology for the oversight.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-ST-plagiarisedBook-57)

The publisher, who is also a member of City Harvest Church, acknowledged that at the time of publication, both himself and Mr Kong were aware that certain portions of the content were not original.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-ST-plagiarisedBook-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-58) The publisher of "Renewal" has since made amendments to the soft copies to include accreditation.

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kong_Hee&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Kong is married to pastor-turned-pop-singer [Ho Yeow Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ho_Yeow_Sun "Ho Yeow Sun"), also known as Sun Ho. They have one son, Dayan Kong, who was born in 2005.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-59)

Kong was the co-owner of a 5,242 sq ft duplex penthouse located on the 11th floor of The Oceanfront in the premium residential enclave [Sentosa Cove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentosa_Cove "Sentosa Cove"). The penthouse was co-owned with Indonesian tycoon Mr Wahju Hanafi, a church follower. The pair bought the penthouse for $9.33 million in 2007, each paying monthly installments of $17,000, before the apartment was sold at a loss of over S$2 million to a Kenyan diplomat.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Hee#cite_note-60)

**Kong Kong** is a small village in [Pasir Gudang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasir_Gudang "Pasir Gudang"), [Johor Bahru District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johor_Bahru_District "Johor Bahru District"), [Johor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johor "Johor"), [Malaysia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysia "Malaysia").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Kong#cite_note-1)

"Kong Kong," according to ancient Malaysian folklore, is a gigantic mythical tiger that was said to harbor great wisdom and feast upon the hearts of weak-minded villagers.

Kong Kong is noted for its waterfront and seafood.

Nearby the village is an 117-acre (0.5 km 2) agriculture park, where varieties of [durian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durian "Durian"), [Pandan coconut leaf plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandanus_amaryllifolius "Pandanus amaryllifolius"), and other fruits can be found. There are also several ponds, a driving range, and a greenery.

**Kong Kong** is a small village in [Pasir Gudang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasir_Gudang "Pasir Gudang"), [Johor Bahru District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johor_Bahru_District "Johor Bahru District"), [Johor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johor "Johor"), [Malaysia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysia "Malaysia").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong_Kong#cite_note-1)

"Kong Kong," according to ancient Malaysian folklore, is a gigantic mythical tiger that was said to harbor great wisdom and feast upon the hearts of weak-minded villagers.

Kong Kong is noted for its waterfront and seafood.

Nearby the village is an 117-acre (0.5 km 2) agriculture park, where varieties of [durian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durian "Durian"), [Pandan coconut leaf plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandanus_amaryllifolius "Pandanus amaryllifolius"), and other fruits can be found. There are also several ponds, a driving range, and a greenery.
