From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This is a **list of religious leaders who have been convicted of serious crimes** before, during or after their period as a religious leader.

## Violent crimes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Violent crimes")]

*   [Tony Alamo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alamo_Christian_Foundation "Alamo Christian Foundation") – Headed a Santa Clarita commune. Convicted of tax evasion in 1994 and then resided in a halfway house in [Texarkana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texarkana "Texarkana").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-1) In 2009, he was convicted of ten federal counts of taking minors across state lines for sex, and sentenced to 150 years in federal prison.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-2)
*   [Shoko Asahara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoko_Asahara "Shoko Asahara") – Founder of [Aum Shinrikyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aum_Shinrikyo "Aum Shinrikyo") sentenced to death by [hanging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanging "Hanging") under [Japanese law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_law "Japanese law") for involvement in the 1995 [Sarin gas attack on the Tokyo subway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarin_gas_attack_on_the_Tokyo_subway "Sarin gas attack on the Tokyo subway").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-3)
*   [Wayne Bent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Bent "Wayne Bent") (aka: Michael Travesser) – Founder of [Lord Our Righteousness Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord_Our_Righteousness_Church "Lord Our Righteousness Church"), sometimes called Strong City. Was convicted of one count of criminal sexual contact of a minor and two counts of contributing to the delinquency of a minor in 2008.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-4) He was sentenced to 18 years with eight years suspended.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-5)
*   [Graham Capill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graham_Capill "Graham Capill") – former leader of [Christian Heritage New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Heritage_New_Zealand "Christian Heritage New Zealand"). Sentenced to a nine-year imprisonment term in 2005 after multiple charges of child sexual abuse against girls younger than twelve.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-6)
*   [Matthew F. Hale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_F._Hale "Matthew F. Hale") – Former leader of [Creativity Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creativity_Movement "Creativity Movement") sentenced to a 40-year prison term for soliciting an undercover FBI informant to kill a federal judge.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-7)
*   [Ahmad Badreddin Hassoun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmad_Badreddin_Hassoun "Ahmad Badreddin Hassoun") – [Grand Mufti of Syria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Mufti_of_Syria "Grand Mufti of Syria") from 2005 until 2021. Sentenced to life imprisonment following the [fall of the Assad regime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_of_the_Assad_regime "Fall of the Assad regime") for crimes including "inciting civil war and sectarian strife", incitement to murder and abuse of office.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-8)
*   [Warren Jeffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Jeffs "Warren Jeffs") – Once President of [Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundamentalist_Church_of_Jesus_Christ_of_Latter_Day_Saints "Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints") (a polygamist Mormon sect), convicted of rape as an accomplice (overturned in 2010). Jeffs was convicted in a Texas state court of child sex charges and sentenced to life plus 20 years. He is incarcerated at the Powledge state prison. He also awaits trial in other states and in the federal court system.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-9)
*   [Jung Myung-seok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jung_Myung-seok "Jung Myung-seok") – South Korean religious sect leader and founder of [Providence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence_(religion) "Providence (religion)"). Convicted for raping several of his followers.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-10)
*   [William Kamm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Kamm "William Kamm") – An Australian religious sect leader who was sentenced to prison in October 2005 for a string of sexual attacks on a 15-year-old girl. In August 2007 his sentence was increased after being found guilty for a series of sexual abuses against another teenage girl over a five-year period.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-11)
*   [Ervil LeBaron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ervil_LeBaron "Ervil LeBaron") – Led a small sect of [polygamous Mormon fundamentalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygamous_Mormon_fundamentalists "Polygamous Mormon fundamentalists"), and was convicted of involvement in the murder of two people and plotting to kill another person in 1981.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-12)
*   [Alice Lenshina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_Lenshina "Alice Lenshina") – Zambian head and founder of the [Lumpa Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lumpa_Church "Lumpa Church"). Conflicts with the government over the sect's rejection of taxes led to a violent confrontation and her subsequent imprisonment.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-13)
*   [Jeffrey Lundgren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_Lundgren "Jeffrey Lundgren") – Headed splinter group from [Reorganized Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reorganized_Church_of_Jesus_Christ_of_Latter_Day_Saints "Reorganized Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints"), executed on October 24, 2006, for multiple murders.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-14)
*   [Charles Manson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Manson "Charles Manson") – Leader of the [Manson Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manson_Family "Manson Family") who served life in prison for [first-degree murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder_in_United_States_law "Murder in United States law") until his death in 2017.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-15)
*   [Shukri Mustafa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shukri_Mustafa "Shukri Mustafa") – Egyptian leader of [Takfir wal-Hijra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takfir_wal-Hijra "Takfir wal-Hijra") who was captured and executed on March 19, 1978, for the kidnapping and murder of an Egyptian ex-government minister.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-16)
*   [Fred Phelps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Phelps "Fred Phelps") – Leader of anti-gay [Westboro Baptist Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westboro_Baptist_Church "Westboro Baptist Church"). Convicted for disorderly conduct and battery.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-18)
*   [Swami Premananda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swami_Premananda_(guru) "Swami Premananda (guru)") – Indian religious leader convicted and sentenced to two life sentences for the rape of 13 girls and murder in 2005.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-19)
*   [Theodore Rinaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodore_Rinaldo "Theodore Rinaldo") – Leader of a religious group in [Snohomish, Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snohomish,_Washington "Snohomish, Washington") convicted of third-degree statutory rape for having sexual intercourse with one minor girl and of taking indecent liberties with another.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-20)
*   [Keith Raniere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Raniere "Keith Raniere") – The founder of NXIVM, a multi-level marketing company and cult based near Albany, New York. Raniere was convicted of racketeering on the charges of sex trafficking, sexual exploitation of a child, attempted sex trafficking, identity theft, forced labor, conspiracy to alter records, conspiracy of sex trafficking, forced labor, racketeering, and wire fraud. Raniere was sentenced to 120 years in federal prison starting in January 2021.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-22)
*   [Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gurmeet_Ram_Rahim_Singh "Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh") – an Indian guru, music producer, singer-songwriter, actor, and filmmaker. He has been the head of the social group [Dera Sacha Sauda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dera_Sacha_Sauda "Dera Sacha Sauda") since 1990. On 28 August 2017, Singh was sentenced to 20 years in jail for rape.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-23) He has also faced prosecution for murder and ordering forced castrations. He is also alleged to have committed sexual assaults on many of his followers. He is also alleged to be involved in the murder of a journalist[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-24)
*   [Flordelis dos Santos de Souza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flordelis_dos_Santos_de_Souza "Flordelis dos Santos de Souza") – Brazilian former Pentecostal pastor, gospel singer and politician. In 2022, she was convicted of murder of her husband, Anderson do Carmo.
*   [Paul Schäfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Sch%C3%A4fer "Paul Schäfer") – Former head of Chile-based [Colonia Dignidad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonia_Dignidad "Colonia Dignidad"), was convicted of sexually abusing 25 children.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-25)
*   [Joseph Smith, Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Smith "Joseph Smith") – The founder of the [Latter Day Saint movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latter_Day_Saint_movement "Latter Day Saint movement"), was "subjected to approximately thirty criminal actions" during his life. Another source reports [Smith was arrested at least 42 times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Smith_and_the_criminal_justice_system "Joseph Smith and the criminal justice system").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-26) A year after committing assault and battery on a local official,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-27) Smith was [killed by a mob](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_of_Joseph_Smith "Death of Joseph Smith") while in jail awaiting trial on charges of treason against Illinois.
*   [Roch Thériault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roch_Th%C3%A9riault "Roch Thériault") – Former head of "Ant Hill Kids commune" served a [life sentence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_sentence "Life sentence") in Canada for the murder of Solange Boislard.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-28)
*   [Yahweh ben Yahweh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yahweh_ben_Yahweh "Yahweh ben Yahweh") – Head of [Nation of Yahweh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nation_of_Yahweh "Nation of Yahweh"), convicted for [Federal racketeering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racketeer_Influenced_and_Corrupt_Organizations_Act "Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act") charges and conspiracy involving 14 murders.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-29)
*   [Dwight York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_York "Dwight York") – Head of [Nuwaubianism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuwaubianism "Nuwaubianism"), convicted in 2004 of multiple [RICO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RICO "RICO"), child molestation, and financial reporting charges and sentenced to 135 years in prison.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-30)

## Non-violent crimes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Non-violent crimes")]

*   [Jim Bakker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Bakker "Jim Bakker") – Created the [PTL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_PTL_Club "The PTL Club") (Praise the Lord) organization. Convicted of [fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraud "Fraud") and conspiracy charges after illegally soliciting millions of dollars from his followers.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-31)
*   [David Yonggi Cho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yonggi_Cho "David Yonggi Cho") – Founder of [Yoido Full Gospel Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoido_Full_Gospel_Church "Yoido Full Gospel Church"). Sentenced to three years in prison in 2014 for embezzling 13 billion won (US$12 million) in church funds.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-32)
*   [Joseph Di Mambro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Di_Mambro "Joseph Di Mambro") – A founder of the [Order of the Solar Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Solar_Temple "Order of the Solar Temple"). Several years prior to founding the group, he was convicted of fraud, impersonating a psychiatrist, and writing bad checks.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-33)
*   [William R. Ferguson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_R._Ferguson "William R. Ferguson") – Founder of the [Cosmic Circle of Fellowship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosmic_Circle_of_Fellowship "Cosmic Circle of Fellowship"). From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This is a **list of religious leaders who have been convicted of serious crimes** before, during or after their period as a religious leader.

## Violent crimes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Violent crimes")]

*   [Tony Alamo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alamo_Christian_Foundation "Alamo Christian Foundation") – Headed a Santa Clarita commune. Convicted of tax evasion in 1994 and then resided in a halfway house in [Texarkana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texarkana "Texarkana").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-1) In 2009, he was convicted of ten federal counts of taking minors across state lines for sex, and sentenced to 150 years in federal prison.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-2)
*   [Shoko Asahara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoko_Asahara "Shoko Asahara") – Founder of [Aum Shinrikyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aum_Shinrikyo "Aum Shinrikyo") sentenced to death by [hanging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanging "Hanging") under [Japanese law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_law "Japanese law") for involvement in the 1995 [Sarin gas attack on the Tokyo subway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarin_gas_attack_on_the_Tokyo_subway "Sarin gas attack on the Tokyo subway").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-3)
*   [Wayne Bent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Bent "Wayne Bent") (aka: Michael Travesser) – Founder of [Lord Our Righteousness Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord_Our_Righteousness_Church "Lord Our Righteousness Church"), sometimes called Strong City. Was convicted of one count of criminal sexual contact of a minor and two counts of contributing to the delinquency of a minor in 2008.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-4) He was sentenced to 18 years with eight years suspended.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-5)
*   [Graham Capill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graham_Capill "Graham Capill") – former leader of [Christian Heritage New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Heritage_New_Zealand "Christian Heritage New Zealand"). Sentenced to a nine-year imprisonment term in 2005 after multiple charges of child sexual abuse against girls younger than twelve.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-6)
*   [Matthew F. Hale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_F._Hale "Matthew F. Hale") – Former leader of [Creativity Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creativity_Movement "Creativity Movement") sentenced to a 40-year prison term for soliciting an undercover FBI informant to kill a federal judge.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-7)
*   [Ahmad Badreddin Hassoun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmad_Badreddin_Hassoun "Ahmad Badreddin Hassoun") – [Grand Mufti of Syria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Mufti_of_Syria "Grand Mufti of Syria") from 2005 until 2021. Sentenced to life imprisonment following the [fall of the Assad regime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_of_the_Assad_regime "Fall of the Assad regime") for crimes including "inciting civil war and sectarian strife", incitement to murder and abuse of office.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_religious_leaders_convicted_of_crimes&wrap=1#cite_note-8)
*   [Warren Jeffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Jeffs "Warren Jeffs") – Once President of [Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundamentalist_Church_of_Jesus_Christ_of_Latter_Day_Saints "Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints") (a polygamist Mormon sect), convicted of rape as an accomplice (overturned in 2010).
